Lemma
[harmonic forms are closed and coclosed]

Source: petersen:page-0349 ↗ def:pet-ch9-hodge-laplacian 1. ch9:9.1.1A form $\omega $ satisfies $\square \omega =0$ precisely when $d\omega =\delta \omega =0$. An exact form with this property is necessarily zero.
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch9-harmonic-iff-closed-coclosed \sketch Adjointness gives

\[ (\square \omega ,\omega )=\| \delta \omega \| _2^2+\| d\omega \| _2^2. \]

Thus a harmonic form is closed and coclosed, and the converse follows from the definition of $\square $. If also $\omega =d\theta $, then $\| \omega \| _2^2=(\theta ,\delta \omega )=0$.

□
